comment: Frozen protocol contracts for docs/implementation-plan.md section 1.3. Every field width is an expression over the profile geometry, never a hand-typed constant, so changing ROB depth or queue depth cannot silently leave an under-sized tag behind. tools/check_contracts.py evaluates the expressions and proves the arithmetic (modulus, ABA bound, compare distance) actually holds for the profile.
rule: Every interface must state one owner, an explicit transfer rule, an explicit cancel rule, an explicit response rule, and at least one resource with a unique allocate and release event. Identity must never be carried by a wrapping index alone: any field that can alias after wrap needs a generation or epoch of its own.

interfaces.name: fetch_decode
interfaces.summary: Instruction fetch requests and their responses, including the original bits and length of every instruction, so a compressed instruction crossing a fetch boundary still reports the PC it belongs to.
interfaces.transfer: valid && ready on both sides; payload must be stable while valid && !ready
interfaces.cancel: A redirect raises the fetch epoch. Outstanding responses carrying an older epoch are dropped at the receiver, and their request slot credit is returned exactly once.
interfaces.response: Responses may arrive out of order. Each response is classified live (epoch matches and the slot is still outstanding), stale (epoch differs) or squashed (slot already recycled); only a live response may be decoded.

identity_fields.name: hart
identity_fields.why: every packet carries its hart; p0/p1 have one, p3 has two

identity_fields.name: pc
identity_fields.why: architectural instruction address

identity_fields.name: req_id
identity_fields.why: identifies the outstanding request slot a response belongs to

identity_fields.name: epoch
identity_fields.why: a req_id alone aliases after wrap; the epoch distinguishes a recycled slot from the request that still owns it

resources.name: fetch_request_slot
resources.release: its response is consumed, or the redirect that raised the epoch cancels it and the cancel is acknowledged

interfaces.credit_return_path: cancel acknowledgement returns the request slot credit
aba_counterexamples: A response for request slot 2 arrives after a redirect recycled slot 2 for a different PC; without the epoch it would be decoded at the wrong PC.
A late response for a squashed branch target is mistaken for a live response and allocates a ROB entry for an instruction that no longer exists.

interfaces.name: macro_dispatch
interfaces.summary: One dispatched macro-instruction, carrying everything needed to place it in the ROB and to route it later.
interfaces.transfer: valid && ready; the whole group is accepted atomically or not at all
interfaces.cancel: A squash marks the ROB entries dead; the macro is not explicitly flushed, it dies with its ROB entries, and any physical tags it allocated are freed only when the allocator observes the squash.
interfaces.response: There is no response; allocation either happens atomically for the whole group or the rename stage back-pressures. A partially allocated group is not representable.

identity_fields.name: hart
identity_fields.why: per-hart ordering domain

identity_fields.name: rob_index
identity_fields.why: slot in the reorder buffer

identity_fields.name: rob_gen
identity_fields.why: the ROB index wraps every rob_entries allocations; the generation makes a recycled slot distinguishable from the macro that still owns it

identity_fields.name: uop_index
identity_fields.why: position within a macro; a macro may own several uops

identity_fields.name: seq
identity_fields.why: age for oldest-first selection; the modulus must exceed twice the largest comparable distance, which is every uop of every live ROB entry

resources.name: rob_entry
resources.release: the macro retires, or a squash kills it

resources.name: physical_register
resources.release: the macro retires and frees the previous mapping, or a squash frees the speculative tag

interfaces.credit_return_path: retire frees the ROB entry and the physical tag in the same architectural order; a squash frees both without retiring
aba_counterexamples: A uop from a squashed macro arrives at an issue queue after its ROB entry has been reallocated; matching on rob_index alone would let it execute and write the new owner's destination register.
Last-uop-arrives-is-treated-as-complete: a macro with three uops whose third uop completes first would be marked done while two uops are still outstanding.

interfaces.name: issue_lease
interfaces.summary: An all-or-nothing grant of the resources one uop needs to run to completion.
interfaces.transfer: One atomic grant or zero grant. There is no partial hold: a uop never waits holding one resource for another, so the wait graph cannot contain a cycle.
interfaces.cancel: A kill removes the uop from the queue before issue. Once a lease is granted the unit must accept it; a unit that cannot accept a granted lease must reserve capacity for it at grant time.
interfaces.response: The grant names the result credit the unit will consume. If no credit is available the grant is not made, so a unit can never stall holding a lease.

identity_fields.name: owner_gen
identity_fields.why: matches the macro's ROB generation; a stale grant cannot write a recycled destination

identity_fields.name: uop_index
identity_fields.why: which uop of the macro holds the lease

identity_fields.name: route_id
identity_fields.why: which cluster was granted, needed to route the result back

resources.name: issue_queue_entry
resources.allocate: dispatch inserts into the target cluster queue
resources.release: the uop is issued under a granted lease, or killed

resources.name: result_credit
resources.allocate: reserved at grant time so the unit can never stall
resources.release: the completion is accepted by the result FIFO

interfaces.credit_return_path: an unissued lease returns its result credit at kill time
aba_counterexamples: A result credit is reserved for a uop that is then killed; without a return path the credit leaks and the fabric eventually deadlocks with free issue-queue entries.
A unit accepts a lease, stalls for a cycle, and a broadcast result from another producer overwrites its destination because ownership was treated as a broadcast rather than exactly-once.

interfaces.name: operand_result
interfaces.summary: A produced value travelling from its unit to the PRF bank that owns it, or as a local bypass to a waiting consumer.
interfaces.transfer: valid && ready; payload stable while stalled
interfaces.cancel: If the producer has been squashed, the result is discarded at writeback and no PRF write occurs.
interfaces.response: exactly-once ownership per destination: a result is written once, not broadcast. A duplicate producer for the same destination tag plus generation is a bug, not a merge.

identity_fields.name: prf_tag
identity_fields.why: 96 physical entries need 7 bits; the depth is deliberately not a power of two, so the free list, not a wrapping pointer, decides allocation

identity_fields.name: prf_gen
identity_fields.why: a tag is recycled; the generation distinguishes the new owner from the old

identity_fields.name: producer_owner_gen
identity_fields.why: the epoch check must respect an older instruction that is still live across a redirect, not blindly reject everything from the previous epoch

resources.name: prf_bank_write_port
resources.allocate: per cycle, one write per bank

interfaces.credit_return_path: a discarded result consumes its reserved credit and returns it
aba_counterexamples: A result from a squashed uop writes the tag that has since been reallocated to a younger uop; the older instruction's value lands in the younger instruction's destination.
Two units complete for the same destination in one cycle and both are written, so the value seen depends on arbitration order rather than on the allocation order.

interfaces.name: memory_request
interfaces.summary: Speculative reads and committed stores travelling to the ordered memory endpoint, plus non-speculative MMIO.
interfaces.transfer: valid && ready with per-id credit; responses may be out of order but each id completes exactly once
interfaces.cancel: A squashed load is cancelled; a committed store is never cancelled because it is already architecturally visible.
interfaces.response: One response per request id, carrying either data or a fault. Late responses for an id that has been reused are rejected by the id plus generation pair.

identity_fields.name: hart
identity_fields.why: per-hart ordering

identity_fields.name: tx_id
identity_fields.why: one outstanding transaction id space shared by fetch, LQ, SQ and MSHRs; the space is rounded up to a power of two, so the width is the ceiling log2 of the number that can be live, not the count itself

identity_fields.name: tx_gen
identity_fields.why: a tx_id alone aliases once it wraps; the modulus exceeds twice the in-flight count so a live response can never be confused with a new request

identity_fields.name: epoch
identity_fields.why: speculative accesses from a squashed path must not be mistaken for live ones

resources.name: memory_transaction_id
resources.allocate: the LSU or the fetch unit issues a transaction

interfaces.credit_return_path: every response returns its transaction id credit, including error responses
aba_counterexamples: A store that has been authorized at commit is squashed by a later redirect and its address is reused; the device sees two writes and the MMIO side effect happens twice.
A load crosses an older store whose address is still unknown, the alias is discovered later, and the load is replayed; a replay without a new generation writes the old value twice.

interfaces.name: completion
interfaces.summary: Notification that a uop, or one element of a vector uop, has produced its result.
interfaces.cancel: A completion whose macro has been squashed is accepted and dropped, so the ROB slot and any reserved credit are still returned.
interfaces.response: None; the ROB entry is updated in place.

identity_fields.name: rob_index
identity_fields.why: which ROB entry

identity_fields.name: rob_gen
identity_fields.why: the ROB index alone aliases after wrap

identity_fields.name: uop_bitmap_index
identity_fields.why: which uop of the macro completed

identity_fields.name: element_index
identity_fields.why: which vector element completed; a vector instruction is not all-or-nothing. The widest case is LMUL=8 with SEW=8 over a VLEN-bit register, giving VLEN elements. This field is inert in profiles that do not implement V

resources.name: completion_bitmap
resources.allocate: the macro's bitmap is cleared at allocation
resources.release: the bitmap is fully set, at which point the macro is complete

interfaces.credit_return_path: completion acceptance returns the uop's issue-queue entry
aba_counterexamples: A completion from a squashed macro sets the bitmap of the macro that has since taken the same ROB entry; the new macro retires without ever executing.
A vector instruction with vl=1 completes its single element and is treated as fully complete when eight elements were expected.

interfaces.name: retire_event
interfaces.summary: The architectural record: per-hart monotonic order with PC, instruction bits, register writes, CSR deltas and trap information.
interfaces.transfer: Append-only stream; the consumer is never back-pressured into changing architectural behaviour
interfaces.cancel: There is none. Once retired, an event is architecturally final and cannot be cancelled.

identity_fields.name: hart
identity_fields.why: per-hart ordering domain

identity_fields.name: retire_seq
identity_fields.why: monotonic per-hart retire counter; the modulus exceeds twice the ROB depth so a wrapped counter is never confused with a live one

identity_fields.name: pc
identity_fields.why: architectural program counter of the retired instruction

resources.name: retire_event_slot
resources.release: when the event tap has consumed it

interfaces.credit_return_path: the event tap returns the slot; the stream is lossless
aba_counterexamples: A trap is emitted as a normal retire, so a reference checker comparing instruction streams sees a phantom instruction.
A store becomes visible to the memory model before its retire event, so a replay from the event stream produces a different memory state than the original run.

interfaces.name: reconfigure
interfaces.summary: Ownership change of an existing resource pool, for example moving a cluster's share of execution units.
interfaces.transfer: Explicit state machine: STOP_ADMIT -> DRAIN -> ACK -> PUBLISH -> RESUME
interfaces.cancel: An aborted reconfiguration returns the resource to its original owner with its original generation; nothing may be reused before the barrier is acknowledged.
interfaces.response: Each participant acknowledges the barrier; ids, credits and state are only recycled after every acknowledgement.

identity_fields.name: old_owner_gen
identity_fields.why: the generation in force before the change

identity_fields.name: new_owner_gen
identity_fields.why: the generation published after the barrier; must differ from the old one

identity_fields.name: outstanding
identity_fields.why: drain count, bounded by every uop of every live ROB entry

resources.name: resource_pool
resources.release: only after the barrier is acknowledged by every participant

interfaces.credit_return_path: drain returns every outstanding credit before publish; an unacknowledged barrier blocks resume
aba_counterexamples: A participant is granted a resource under the new generation before the barrier is acknowledged, and a late drain from the old generation frees it.
Reconfiguration is aborted after some participants have already published, and the two halves of the pool disagree about the owner generation.
